cards.text: It's Pentecost in Jerusalem. The Holy Spirit just came on Jesus' followers, they're speaking languages they never learned, and some folks in the crowd are saying they're drunk. Then Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, stands up with the other eleven, lifts up his voice and tells the whole crowd to listen carefully.

cards.question: Peter's first point to the crowd: these men are NOT drunk, the way people suppose. What reason does he give?

answers.text: It's only the third hour of the day
They have been in the temple all night
They are speaking far too clearly for that

cards.text: The third hour of the day? Friend, at that hour I'm still ARGUING with my snooze button. No, Peter says, this is what was spoken by Joel, one of God's prophets.

cards.question: In the words Peter quotes from Joel, God says that in the last days He will pour out His Spirit on the priests and nobody else.

cards.text: It's ALL people: sons and daughters prophesy, young men see visions, old men dream dreams, and God pours out His Spirit even on menservants and maidservants. God is NOT checking anybody's job title at the door.

Then Joel's words turn to the sky: wonders in the heavens, signs on the earth, blood and fire and billows of smoke. The sun turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the great and glorious Day of the Lord.

cards.question: After all those signs, Joel's words end with a promise: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be ___.

cards.text: Now Peter turns to the Man at the center of it all: Jesus of Nazareth. God certified Him with miracles, wonders and signs right among these people, and Peter says they know it themselves.

cards.question: Peter says Jesus was delivered up by a set plan and foreknowledge. Whose?

cards.text: And Peter doesn't tiptoe. He tells this crowd that they, by the hands of the lawless, put Jesus to death by nailing Him to the cross.

cards.question: Peter says God raised Jesus from the dead, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.

cards.text: Then Peter quotes David, Israel's king, and says David is talking about Jesus: ‘I saw the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.’

cards.question: David's heart is glad and his body will dwell in hope, because God will not abandon his soul to Hades, nor let His Holy One see ___.

cards.text: David's words end with joy in God's presence, but Peter reminds them that David died, was buried, and his tomb is with them to this day. So if David meant himself, friend, we've got a problem, because everybody knows EXACTLY where he is.

cards.question: Peter says David was a prophet, and God had promised him on oath to put one of his descendants on his throne. So who was David really talking about?

answers.text: The Christ rising from the dead
His son Solomon on the throne

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd he's the only one who can vouch that God raised Jesus to life.
Peter says Jesus is exalted to the right hand of God and received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father. So who has poured out what the crowd now sees and hears?

cards.text: David never ascended into heaven, Peter says. But David himself says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’

cards.question: Peter's big finish: let all Israel know with certainty that God has made this Jesus, whom they crucified, both ___ and ___.

cards.text: Peter's done preaching, and it LANDS. When the people hear this, they're cut to the heart.

cards.question: Cut to the heart, what does the crowd ask Peter and the other apostles?

answers.text: Brothers why did no one warn us

cards.question: Peter's answer is for every one of them. What two things does he tell them to do?
Peter tells them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of their ___.

cards.text: And they'll receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, the same Spirit this crowd just watched get poured out. Friend, that's not a free sample, that's the WHOLE cookie box.

cards.question: Peter says this promise belongs only to the people standing in front of him that day.

cards.text: It's for them, their children, and all who are far off, all whom the Lord our God will call. With many other words Peter keeps testifying, and he urges them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”

cards.question: Peter's message falls flat, and only a handful of people are baptized that day.

cards.text: Those who embraced his message were baptized, and about THREE THOUSAND were added to the believers that day. Friend, my biggest day welcoming newcomers to the junk drawer was a rubber band and a twist tie.

cards.question: The new believers devote themselves to the apostles' ___ and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to ___.

cards.text: A sense of awe comes over everyone, and the apostles perform many wonders and signs. All the believers are together and have everything in common.

cards.question: When anyone among them is in need, the believers sell their possessions and goods and share with them.

cards.text: Every day, with one accord, they meet in the temple courts and break bread from house to house, with gladness and sincerity of heart. Thousands of people with one accord, and I've watched a group chat of SIX fall apart over one emoji.

cards.question: They're praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And what does the Lord do, day after day?

answers.text: Adds to their number those being saved
Opens prison doors for the apostles
Gives them a new language to speak

findings.problem: The opening card retells events from the previous passage (Acts 2:1-13): the Holy Spirit coming on Jesus' followers, the unlearned languages, and the crowd saying they're drunk (Acts 2:13). It cites only Acts 2:14. One rule says to cite every verse a card uses, first to last. Another says to give context when a passage starts mid-thought. Following the first would put the citation outside the stop's range and outside the passage.
findings.question: When the opening card gives context from the passage before it, should its 'verses' include those earlier verses (e.g. 'Acts 2:1-14'), cite them some other way, or stay limited to the passage's own verses?

findings.problem: The choice cards in stop 1 follow a fixed cycle: MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, then MC, FB (cards 2, 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19). The question types repeat in a set order instead of being chosen naturally for each card.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: This fill-in-the-blank asks the baker to supply the next word of David's poetic line ('nor let His Holy One see ___'). The baker hasn't seen that wording and can't reason it out from earlier cards. 'darkness' also sits close to the idea of Hades, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup joke ('So if David meant himself, friend, we've got a problem, because everybody knows EXACTLY where he is') rules out the wrong answer 'Himself in his old age' on card 15. It also hands over Peter's reasoning before the baker is asked for it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Peter's done preaching' contradicts the text. Peter keeps speaking in Acts 2:38-40 ('With many other words he testified'), and stop 2 card 7 says he keeps testifying.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'When anyone among them is in need' narrows the text. Acts 2:45 says they 'shared with anyone who was in need' and doesn't limit it to people among the believers.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Every day... they meet in the temple courts and break bread from house to house' attaches 'daily' to the house-to-house bread breaking as well. Acts 2:46 puts 'daily' with meeting in the temple courts and doesn't clearly give a time for breaking bread.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
